April 1 to March 31, labelled by the starting year, e.g. 2023-24

[PMAY] Resolver rule: How to derive financial year
CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sanction_date) >= 4 THEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM sanction_date) ELSE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM sanction_date) - 1 END

[PMAY] Resolver rule: Rows that belong to no financial year
126 records have a NULL sanction_date and belong to NO financial year. They are excluded from every FY figure. 171107 total - 126 = 170981, which is exactly the sum of the houses column in the FY summary.

[PMAY] Resolver rule: Incomplete financial year coverage

[PMAY] Resolver rule: This resolver overrides the stage-2 schema on financial year
The stage2 schema says no financial-year column exists and warns against inventing FY semantics. That is correct about pmay_beneficiaries, but the companion PMAY_FullyMapped_FY_summary.xlsx DOES define financial years, and the derivation above reproduces it exactly. FY questions are therefore answerable - derive, do not invent.

[PMAY] Resolver rule: Relative financial year words like latest and previous
latest / current / most recent: 2023-24 previous / last year: 2022-23 earliest / first: 2017-18 all years / overall / since inception / till date: no date filter at all

[PMAY] Resolver rule: How to derive calendar year
EXTRACT(YEAR FROM sanction_date)

[PMAY] Resolver rule: Why year disambiguation is ambiguous
A bare year means different things and the gap is large. Calendar 2023 has 110890 records; FY 2023-24 has 106527. Calendar 2022 has 4056; FY 2022-23 has 8225 - more than double. Silently choosing one is a wrong answer roughly half the time.

[PMAY] Resolver rule: How to read a year disambiguation
(1) A hyphenated or slashed year ("2023-24", "2023/24", "FY 2023") is a FINANCIAL year. (2) The words "financial year", "FY", "fiscal" force the financial year reading. (3) A bare four-digit year ("in 2023", "during 2022") defaults to CALENDAR year, because sanction_date is a plain date and stage2 defines the default that way. State the assumption in the answer. (4) If the question compares against the FY summary figures, or asks about "utilisation", "completion rate" or "pending amount", use the FINANCIAL year - those metrics are defined per FY in the summary table. (5) When the phrasing is genuinely unclear and the two readings differ materially, ask.

[PMAY] Resolver rule: Dates outside the data span
Anything before 2017-08-09 or after 2023-07-04 has no records. Say so with the actual data span rather than returning an empty result with no explanation.

[PMAY] Resolver rule: Month and quarter phrasing
Accept "January 2023", "Jan 23", "Q1 2023" and similar. Convert to an explicit half-open date range. Quarters are calendar quarters unless the user says "financial quarter", in which case Q1 = April-June.

[PMAY] Resolver rule: Hard rules that override everything else
(1) Every stored dimension value in this dataset is Title Case. Compare case-folded and emit the exact stored Title Case form. (2) Villages are resolved by mapped_village_lgd_code, never by name alone. 198 village names are shared by two or more different villages. (3) The word sanctioned is dangerously overloaded - it is a house_status value, a measure (sanctioned_amount) and a date (sanction_date). See overloaded_terms. (4) A bare year is ambiguous between calendar year and financial year, and the two give materially different answers. See year_disambiguation. Ask. (5) reg_no is NOT unique (368 duplicates) and sanction_no is very much NOT unique (35131 distinct across 171107 rows). Never treat either as a primary key. id is. (6) NULL is missing, never zero. 462 rows have no installment/release recorded and 126 rows have no sanction date or amount. (7) If more than one candidate survives, return ambiguous and ask. Never pick the first row. (8) If nothing matches above the fuzzy floor, return not_found with suggestions. Never invent a district, block, village, status or category.

[PMAY] Resolver rule: The pre-aggregate table pmay_fy_summary
pmay_fy_summary holds 7 rows, one row per sanction financial year, from PMAY_FullyMapped_FY_summary.xlsx.
A pre-aggregate of pmay_beneficiaries, NOT a join target. Every column reproduces exactly from the detail table using the financial_year derivation. Use it to answer FY-level questions cheaply, or to sanity-check a detail query - never join the two.
Columns: sanction_fy is financial year label, e.g. 2023-24; houses is COUNT(*) for that FY; sanctioned_cr is SUM(sanctioned_amount) / 10000000, in CRORE rupees; released_cr is SUM(amount_released) / 10000000, in CRORE rupees; completed is COUNT(*) WHERE house_status = 'Completed'; pending_cr is sanctioned_cr - released_cr; completion_pct is completed / houses * 100; utilisation_pct is released_cr / sanctioned_cr * 100.
UNIT WARNING: The _cr columns are in CRORE, while sanctioned_amount and amount_released in the detail table are in RUPEES. 1 crore = 10,000,000. Never compare or add across the two without converting, and always state the unit in the answer.
170981, not 171107 - the 126 dateless records are absent. If the user asks for an all-time total, decide whether to use the detail table (171107 records) or the FY summary (170981) and say which.

[PMAY] Resolver rule: This dataset needs no joins
one row per beneficiary-sanction-house record
pmay_beneficiaries is self-contained. pmay_fy_summary is a pre-aggregate of it, not a join target - see fy_summary_table. Never invent a join to MGNREGA or any other scheme.

[PMAY] Resolver rule: Ways users name the PMAY-G scheme
Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin is called: PMAY, PMAYG, PMAY-G, PMAY G, PM Awas, PM Awaas, Awas Yojana, Awaas Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana, housing scheme, rural housing scheme, PM housing scheme, gramin housing, IAY, Indira Awaas Yojana.
